description: Bugsy's scope for every feature in feature-taxonomy.json. This is the one feature list shared by the PRD (docs/prd.md) and the competitor crosswalk. Everything in scope ships in one build; there are no phases. Change a feature's scope here, then rebuild the PRD site.

plans.In scope: In scope for the first build

positioning.table-stakes: Most competitors have it; buyers expect it on day one
positioning.wedge: Few or no competitors fully support it; part of Bugsy's pitch

specs.01: Foundation: tenancy, auth, roles, branches, audit
specs.02: Customers: accounts, properties, contacts, leads, quotes
specs.03: Catalog: service types, price book, product master
specs.07: Compliance: credentials, records, notices, state rules
specs.08: Billing: Stripe Connect, invoices, autopay, sales tax
specs.09: General ledger: chart of accounts, posting, deferred revenue
specs.14: Commercial programs: devices, maps, trends, audits
specs.15: Specialty services: termite, wildlife, bed bug
specs.17: Sales and growth: door-to-door, commissions, campaigns
specs.18: Inventory, job costing, time and payroll export
specs.19: Routing and fleet: route optimization, GPS
specs.20: Integrations and API: QuickBooks sync, webhooks, phone systems

features.note: Pipeline stages from lead to signed.
Source is required on every lead; close rate by source in the owner dashboard.
Quotes with good, better, best options.
The signature also captures consent to electronic notices and delivers any required pre-application offer.
Territory map, knock outcomes, quick quote, e-sign and card capture at the door.
Rules for reps and technicians, with holds and chargebacks on early cancellation.
Sequences for open quotes, renewals, seasonal upsells and win-backs.
Cancellation reason codes and save offers in the cancellation flow.
An account pays; a property is where work happens; residents are contacts on the property.
Through integrations with phone systems (caller pop, click to call, call logs), not a built-in phone service.
Monthly, every other month, quarterly and custom cadences.
A fixed number of rounds inside a date window, for mosquito and tick seasons.
Size tiers and add-ons maintained centrally.
Yearly increases applied in bulk with customer notice.
Term, auto-renew and optional early cancellation fee per agreement; renewal list 30 days ahead.
Termite warranties with yearly renewal billing; revenue spread over the warranty year.
Re-services are $0 visits on the agreement, with labor and product cost captured.
The whole term is generated as planned visits, each in a due window.
Technician rows by day columns, plus a map pane.
Automatic sequencing and assignment with time windows and workload balancing.
License, certification category and expiry enforced at dispatch for every state, not just skill matching.
Customers book and reschedule in the portal within rules the office sets.
Technician location from the app for dispatchers and on-the-way texts; vehicle telematics through integrations.
Move a technician's whole day at once, for weather.
Native wrapper versus installable web app is decision 4.
Full visit capture with no signal; zero lost visits is a launch metric.
Products picked from the catalog fill in EPA numbers; missing record fields block completion.
Device and station barcodes for commercial programs, plus product labels.
Cash, check, card on file, texted pay links and card readers; readers and tap to pay need the native wrapper.
Clock in and out, feeding the payroll export.
Truck stock, transfers and usage deducted from visit records.
Every field the tenant's state requires, locked at day end, corrected only by amendment.
Shared master list with EPA number, active ingredients, restricted-use flag, REI, label and SDS.
Certification categories and expiry, license year, trainee rules; expiry alerts.
Inspector export for a date range, plus state report formats as each state's rule pack adds them.
Post-application, pre-application, resident, posting and registry notices as state rules require, each with proof of sending.
Restricted-use products only for licensed, certified applicators, never trainees working alone.
Stock by branch and truck, receipts, transfers and usage, feeding chemical inventory in the ledger.
Each state's rules kept as data (record fields, notice timing, registries, posting, blackouts); launch states are decision 2.
Moving or adding a device updates the map in the same step.
One-click audit binder for a date range.
Customers add sightings in the portal; recommendations tracked to a closed date.
PO numbers, net terms, per-site or consolidated invoices.
Property diagrams, bait station checks, WDI reports and warranty renewals.
Multi-visit trapping, exclusion and repair jobs with materials and landowner authorization; seasonal blackouts such as bat exclusion windows come from state rules.
Multi-visit treatments with customer prep checklists.
Mosquito and tick seasons through seasonal programs; taxability set per service type.
Stripe Connect, one connected account per tenant.
Card and ACH saved on file.
Per visit, flat monthly and annual prepay, chosen per agreement.
Taxability by service type, rate by service address.
Reminders, retries, late fees and a past-due flag that can pause service.
One statement per account across agreements.
Settle the contract balance on cancellation; the cancellation fee is its own line.
Double-entry ledger per tenant with a pest chart of accounts.
Summarized journal sync to QuickBooks Online for tenants who keep their books there.
Xero, Sage and NetSuite adapters wait for demand; QuickBooks covers most small pest companies.
Contract balance per agreement: deferred revenue or unbilled receivable, matching the ledger fixtures.
Labor from visit times and product cost from usage; margin by visit, account, route, technician and service line.
Payroll is not built: export hours, production pay and commissions, and post the payroll journal back.
Pay, update card, see visit history, products applied and notices, request a re-service.
Included in the base price; at least six of nine competitors charge extra for texting.
Office and customer text back and forth on the account timeline.
Automatic review request after a completed visit.
The post-service summary doubles as the post-application notice when the customer consented.
Owner dashboard and standard reports.
Retention and cancellations by service line, route and technician. PestPac and FieldRoutes announced churn analytics in October 2026.
Stops per day, revenue per technician, time on site and re-service rate.
Saved custom reports and a data export for BI tools.
Each branch is a licensed business location.
Default roles that tenants copy and adjust.
Public API and webhooks, so AI receptionists and assistants can connect.
Spreadsheet import with dry run; importers for specific pest software come later.
Service summaries drafted from technician notes, product amount checks against the label, churn risk, and portal answers from the customer's own history.
Embeddable lead and booking forms and an intake endpoint; hosted websites are out of scope.
Direct mail, call tracking and SEO are services, not product; connect through the API instead.
